'''''Catananche caerulea''''', or '''Cupid's dart''', is a greyish green [[perennial plant|perennial]] [[herbaceous plant]] with a basal leaf rosette and conspicuous blue-purple or sometimes white flowerheads, belonging to the [[Asteraceae|daisy family]]. It is a popular garden plant and is often used in dried flower arrangements.<ref name=CP>{{cite book|last= Sell|first= P.D.|year= 1976|chapter= 147. Catananche L.|page= 305|editor= Tutin, G. & al.|title= Flora Europaea|volume= 4|location= Cambridge}} and {{cite book|last1= Sell|first1= P.D.|last2= Murell|first2= G.|year= 2006|title= Flora of Great Britain and Ireland|volume= 4|location= Cambridge}} cited on {{cite web|website= Cichorieae Portal|title= Catananche caerulea|url= http://cichorieae.e-taxonomy.net/portal/cdm_dataportal/taxon/ca6eb087-bf6e-492d-8866-d177478896b2}}</ref>

It is [[native plant|native]] to the Mediterranean region. The flower was supposedly used by the [[Ancient Greece|ancient Greeks]] as a key ingredient in a [[love potion]], hence the common name "[[Cupid]]'s dart".
[[Image:Catananche caerulea4.jpg|thumb|right|220px]]

== Description ==
[[File:Catananche.jpg|thumb|left|flowerbud]]
[[File:C.c.-cips-1.jpg|thumb|left|cypselas]]Cupid's dart is a short-lived [[Perennial plant|perennial]] [[herbaceous plant]], of 20–90 cm (8-36 in) high.<ref name=CP /> It has eighteen [[chromosome]]s (2n=18).<ref>{{cite book|title= Flora Europaea Check – List and Chromosome Index|volume= 1|first= D.M.|last= Moore|publisher= Cambridge University Press|year= 1982|isbn= 9780521237598}}</ref>

=== Leaves and stems ===
There is a basal [[Rosette (botany)|rosette]] of many linear leaves of 2–20 cm long and .25-.75 cm wide, which may be entire or are [[Pinnation|pinnately incised]], creating linear lobes mostly directed towards the tip. The leaves are covered in long soft woolly hairs (pilose) lying on the surface, giving both leaf surfaces a greyish green color. The leaf tips may be blunt or pointy, and the leaf blade gradually narrows to the main vein at the base of the leaf. From the heart of the rosette one or a few, strongly branched, erect, again woolly haired and greyish green flowering stems rise. These stems carry only a few leaves, similar to the basal leaves, but up to 30 cm long, with up to four lateral lobes.<ref name=CP />

=== Flowerheads, florets and fruits ===
Flowerheads are set individually at the end of a branch of up to 30 cm long, with a few small papery bracts, more densely set near the flowerhead. Flowerheads are enclosed in an [[Bract#Involucral bracts|involucre]] of 1.5–2.5 cm long, which has a diameter of 1–2 cm. The individual bracts are papery, egg-shaped, 1–2.5 cm long, 0.3–0.5 cm wide, hairless and ending abruptly in a small sharp point as a continuation of the darker colored midrib. The common base at which the florets are implanted (or [[Asteraceae#Floral heads|receptacle]]) is flat, with a [[Asteraceae#Floral structures|scale subtending every floret]]. The [[Asteraceae#Floral heads|ligulate florets]] have a bluish purple strap ending in five teeth, 2.5–2.9 cm long, while the tube is darker. The one-seeded [[Dehiscence (botany)|indehiscent]] fruit (called [[Asteraceae#Fruits and seeds|cypsela]]) is cylindrical with five to ten longitudinal ribs, 5–6 mm long, and is crowned with papery [[Pappus (flower structure)|pappus scales]].<ref name=CP /> The pollen is yellow.

== Etymology ==
[[File:The Botanical Magazine, Plate 293 (Volume 9, 1795).png|thumb|right|etching]]The simple translation of the root words from the Greek κατάνάγκη (katanagkē), itself a contraction of κατά (kata), "down" and άνάγκη (anagkē), "force", is "compulsion", which is suggested to refer to the use of this plant in love potions,<ref>{{cite web |website=Merriam-Webster Dictionary |title=Catananche|url=https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/catananche |access-date=2016-12-22}}</ref> and is reflected in the vernacular name Cupid's dart.<ref>{{cite web |website=The Garden Helper |title=Cupid's Darts, How to Grow and Care for Cupid's Dart Plant |url=http://www.thegardenhelper.com/catananche.html}}</ref> The species [[epithet]] ''caerulea'' is the Latin for "(heavenly) blue".<ref>{{cite web|website= LatDict|title= caeruleus, caerulea, caeruleum|url= http://latin-dictionary.net/definition/7370/caeruleus-caerulea-caeruleum|access-date= 2017-01-28}}</ref>

== Distribution ==
Cupid's dart occurs in the wild in western North-Africa (Morocco, Algeria, Tunisia and Libya) and south-western Europe (Portugal, Spain including the [[Balearic Islands]], Andorra, France, and Italy). It is naturalized in Czechoslovakia and may temporarily occur elsewhere when it escapes from cultivation.<ref name=CP />

== Ecology ==
''Catananche caerulea'' naturally occurs on disturbed, young or eroded, carbonaceous soils, in plant communities consisting of dwarf shrubs and perennials. It is often associated with different [[Cistaceae]] such as ''[[Fumana laevipes]]'', ''[[Helianthemum apenninum]]'', ''[[Helianthemum cinereum|H. cinereum]]'', ''[[Helianthemum marifolium|H. marifolium]]'', ''[[Helianthemum croceum|H. croceum]]'', several [[Lamiaceae]] such as ''[[Lavandula latifolia]]'', ''[[Rosmarinus palaui]]'', ''[[Teucrium capitulatum]]'', and [[Teucrium haenseleri|T. haenseleri]], several [[Asteraceae]] such as ''[[Rhaponticum coniferum]]'', ''[[Scorzonera hispanica]]'', ''[[Serratula flavescens]]'' and ''[[Serratula pinnatifida|S. pinnatifida]]'', few [[Fabaceae]] like ''[[Astragalus (plant)|Astragalus]] glaux'' and ''[[Ononis pusilla]]'', parasites such as ''[[Cytinus ruber]]'' and ''[[Orobanche latisquama]]'', and other species such as ''[[Aristolochia pistolochia]]'', ''[[Euphorbia nicaeensis]]'', ''[[Globularia vulgaris]]'', ''[[Ruta chalepensis]]'', and ''[[Viola arborescens]]''.<ref>{{cite journal|author= J.C. Costa|display-authors=et al|year= 2012|title= Vascular Plant Communities in Portugal (Continental, the Azores and Madeira)|journal= International Journal of Geobotanical Science|volume= 2|pages= 1–180|url= http://www.repository.utl.pt/handle/10400.5/6250|access-date= 2017-01-28}}</ref>

== Cultivation ==
''Catananche caerulea'' is grown in the garden as an ornamental short-lived perennial, which may re-seed spontaneously. It prefers full sun with good drainage. It is drought tolerant.

Several selections are grown, among which 'Amor Blue', 'Major', with larger flowers, 'Alba' and 'Amor White', white with purple floret tubes.<ref>{{cite web|website= Folia|title= Cupid's dart variety & cultivar list|url= https://myfolia.com/plants/1964-cupids-dart-catananche-caerulea/varieties}}</ref> The [[cultivar]] ''C. caerulea'' 'Major' has gained the [[Royal Horticultural Society]]'s [[Award of Garden Merit]].<ref>{{cite web|title=RHS Plant Selector - ''Catananche caerulea '' 'Major'|url=https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/82052/Catananche-caerulea-Major/Details | access-date=15 April 2020}}</ref> 
(confirmed 2017).<ref>{{cite web  | url= https://www.rhs.org.uk/plants/pdfs/agm-lists/agm-ornamentals.pdf | title = AGM Plants - Ornamental | date = July 2017 | page = 16 | publisher = Royal Horticultural Society | access-date = 24 January 2018}}</ref>
